newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan plans to enact laws for economic reforms.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan plans to enact laws for economic reforms.

text.p: Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's government plans to enact laws for an upcoming structural economic reforms package, the central bank chief said.

The structural reforms will cover all aspects of the economy, including tax and tariff structure, tax administration, expenditure controls, loan recoveries and autonomy of the State (central) Bank of Pakistan, bank governor Muhammad Yaqub told a meeting of senior bankers on Saturday.
"These reforms were discussed in several meetings chaired by the prime minister and are expected to be announced soon."
Yaqub said the reforms would be supplemented by conversion of several ordinances issued by a previous caretaker government into permanent laws.

Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said on Friday the International Monetary Fund (IMF) had suspended a standby loan to Pakistan but had agreed to negotiate a new structural adjustent loan on the basis of the proposed reforms package.
An IMF mission that spent two weeks reviewing Pakistan's economic performance left on Friday without a public statement.

"When the key elements of this reform package were explained to the IMF, a consensus developed that these bold steps were qualitatively substantial and had so much structural content in them that these did not fit into the mould of the existing standby arrangement," Yaqub said.
A successful implementation of structural economic reforms would help in the resumption of the IMF's financial assistance under a new arrangement, he said.
